Our students are part-time, online, and on their phones
1,219
students at CAMP in fall 2024
74%
attend part-time
64%
took at least one online course
48%
are under 18, mostly dual enrollment
91%
of U.S. adults own a smartphone
Set dual enrollees aside and about half of our students are 22 or older: working adults and parents who need answers in three taps between shifts.
For 16% of U.S. adults, the phone is their only internet at home.
Sources: VCCS fall 2019 to 2024 enrollment profile for CAMP; Pew Research Center mobile fact sheet, 2026
3
The vision
One app. One sign-in. Every CAMP service.
A single front door with wrap-around services that makes communication simpler for everyone, and carries our story to the platforms people already use.
One front door, wrap-around services
Student Information System
Register, drop, holds, balance
Canvas
Courses, due dates, announcements
Navigate360
Advising appointments, to-dos
Email, calendar, Teams
Microsoft 365 messages
Payments
Official College payment page
CAMP Connect
One app One VCCS sign-in Phone, tablet, desktop
For students, faculty, staff, leadership, partners, and community
Camp Alert (Everbridge)
Alerts, check-in, roll call
Help and support offices
Book, call, or chat
Campus Feed
Moderated posts and comments
Social media share-out
LinkedIn, Facebook, X, Instagram
Foundation giving
Scholarships and student aid
Each service stays in the system that owns it; CAMP Connect signs people in once and brings it to them

7
Safety: alert and roll call in one tap
Send by building, campus, or the whole College
“I’m safe” or “I need help” on every phone
Live count for Security, building by building
Everbridge stays the official alert system
Building check-in is opt-in, records only the building, and is deleted every night
8
Campus Feed: safe to post, easy to share
Checked before it posts
  • Blocks profanity and personal information
  • Holds threats for Campus Safety and crisis signs for Counseling
  • Holds insults, test-answer requests, outside links, and student photos for review
  • Anyone can report; faculty, deans, and Operations review
Shared out with CAMP branding
  • LinkedIn, Facebook, X, Threads in one tap; copied captions for Instagram and TikTok
  • Only posts the author marks Shareable; dual-enrolled minors’ posts stay inside CAMP
9
Help, feature requests, and feedback built in
A Help button on every screen
  • Ask a question or reach the IT Help Desk in one tap
  • Report a problem: the screen is filled in, a screenshot is optional, and a ticket number comes back
Users help set the roadmap
  • Request a feature; others vote; status shows New, Planned, In progress, Done
  • Rate ease of use from 1 to 5, with an option to send without a name
  • A Feedback inbox for Operations and deans, reviewed every month

11
CAMP owns it and runs it
Our name and listing
Published as “CAMP Connect” under CAMP’s Apple and Google accounts
Our accounts
Registered to CAMP mailboxes, with two College admins on each
Our data
Stored in a U.S. region; check-ins deleted nightly; no card numbers
Our admin console
Offices change links, dates, alerts, and moderation without a developer
A full audit log
Every alert, every look at check-in data, every settings change
An exit plan
Internal: CAMP owns the code. Vendor: guaranteed data export in the contract
Run by an executive sponsor, a steering group, and an IT product owner office, so it never depends on one person.
12
Building it ourselves needs far less cash
A. Vendor platform
Year 1 cash
about $70,000
Five-year cash
about $221,000
Five years with staff time
about $281,000
B. Internal build (recommended)
Year 1 cash
about $39,000
Five-year cash
about $91,000
Five years with staff time
about $211,000
Planning estimates. The vendor figure is based on public Modo Labs contracts; we would need a CAMP quote. Camp Alert (Everbridge) stays under both options.
13
Enrollment upside: 13 to 41 FTE a year
Low
13 FTE
24 more students
$67,060 in tuition and fees a year
Medium
25 FTE
47 more students
$128,963 in tuition and fees a year
High
41 FTE
76 more students
$211,499 in tuition and fees a year
Break-even: about 8 FTE, roughly 15 more students, covers the Year 1 cost.
From better retention, new students reached by the public front door, and more dual enrollees continuing at CAMP. In a randomized study, reminder texts raised community college persistence by 12 points; we assume only 2 to 6.
Sources: VCCS fall 2024 profile for CAMP; CAMP fall 2025 rate of $171.95 per credit; Castleman and Page (The Chronicle)
